description:
Create a draft journal entry (voucher type Journal Entry) of the assigned company; a person reviews and submits it in ERPNext. Give 2 to 20 `accounts` rows, each with exactly one of `debit` and `credit`; debits and credits must be equal. Accounts are in the company's currency. A receivable or payable account needs `party_type` and `party`; ERPNext saves a party on another account but refuses it on submit. A row referencing an invoice carries its party and its receivable or payable account; `reference_type` and `reference_name` come together. `cheque_no` and `cheque_date` (the bank's reference and its date) come together. `posting_date` defaults to today. A draft with the same posting date and rows is refused unless `allow_duplicate` is true. After an error or a timeout, list the drafts (`list_journal_entries` with `state` draft) before creating again: the first may have been saved.

description:
Create a draft purchase invoice of the assigned company from a supplier's invoice; a person reviews and submits it in ERPNext. Give `bill_no` and `bill_date` as printed on the supplier's invoice, and each item's `rate` from it. The draft never updates stock. `posting_date` defaults to today, `due_date` to the supplier's payment terms, counted from `bill_date` when given; for a bill older than its terms, ERPNext refuses its own count, so give the bill's `due_date`. A `bill_no` already recorded for the supplier, in a draft or a submitted invoice, is refused unless `allow_duplicate` is true; without `bill_no`, a draft with the same supplier, posting date and items is. A rate a pricing rule replaced, and an `expense_account` ERPNext replaced, are named in `warnings`. After an error or a timeout, list the drafts (`list_purchase_invoices` with `state` draft) before creating again: the first may have been saved.

description:
The assigned company's General Ledger from `from_date` to `to_date` (at most 366 days), one record per ledger entry, oldest first. Narrow it by `account`, `party_type` with `party`, or `voucher_no`. With `account` or `party`, `opening` is the balance before `from_date` and each record carries its running `balance`; without, `opening` holds only entries marked as opening (such as an Opening Entry), which are never among the records, and `balance` is null. `totals` cover every record, not only this page. Amounts are in `currency`: the company's, or the account's or party's when ERPNext switched to it. A busy ledger may be too large for a year without `account`: narrow it by account or period.
